segments: 253. Chronography of Barhebraeus.
beside his father Chaghri Beg,
after he made a will,
that his son Malik-Shah should reign in his place,
and that the emir Qawurd Beg his brother should marry Khatun his wife,
and should possess the region of Shiraz,
except for those fortresses which properly ought to be under the sultan's command.
Now Qawurd Beg, who had long been waiting for his brother's death,
when he heard that he was dead,
rose up in haste from Kirman,
and traveled by sea in the winter season,
and came to Shiraz,
and set out for Khorasan,
and gathered an army to meet Malik-Shah, his nephew.
Then Malik-Shah prepared for battle with his uncle,
and God gave him the victory, and he was victorious;
and he captured his uncle and killed him,
and he blinded his sons.
Two of the younger ones among them died,
and three lived while blind:
Sultan-Shah, Turkan-Shah, and Wardan-Shah.
And if he had remained in his place,
as the sultan his brother [wished], his honor would have been magnified.
And in the year 466 of the Arabs [= 1073-1074 AD],
which is the year 1384
of the Greeks (1072 of our Lord?),
incessant rains began,
from the Latter Tishri until the twenty-fourth of Shebat.
And the rivers flooded,
and water burst forth from the houses of Baghdad, cleaving open the ground as it came out,
and many courts were demolished.
And the people fled to the western quarter.
And the waters entered the palace of the Caliph from the Gate of Nubia,
that is to say, Nubian eunuchs were guarding that gate.
And the eunuchs and the maidservants fled,
and all those who were in the houses inside the palace—
there were at that time one thousand and five hundred houses in it—
and they departed by swimming,
and went to the western side and took shelter in the houses of the common people.
And when the water sprang up from under the Caliph's bed,
he fled toward the door,
and could not find a way out.
And a eunuch carried him and placed him in a boat (zawraq),
and likewise his wives,
and some of the things that they managed {OCR?} to rescue from drowning.
And the Caliph put on the cloak of their prophet,
and took the staff in his hand,
as if to hold back the violence of the water;
but it availed nothing.
